One 16x16 straight conveyor belt tile, authored from the master palette by art/tools/make-factory-parts.mjs. Hand-authored after two paid Retro Diffusion takes came back as a featureless dark rectangle with the run pointing the wrong way. The deciding reason is not quality: a belt tile must repeat along its run with NO SEAM, and a mismatched edge repeats every 16px down a straight line. `tile_x` is a best effort; the modulus in that script is exact, and it asserts left edge equals right edge on every build.

One 16x16 conveyor belt corner tile — in from the left edge, out through the bottom edge — authored from the master palette by art/tools/make-factory-parts.mjs. Hand-authored after two paid takes; the second came back as a brown scribble on a background that quantised to violet. Drawn as a solid plate rather than a cutout, matching the straight tile: a belt corner is machinery sitting on the ground, not a decal floating over it.

One 16x16 grabber arm, drawn pointing EAST and centred, authored from the master palette by art/tools/make-factory-parts.mjs. Hand-authored after two paid takes returned an inkblot with no claw. The structural reason it stays hand-authored: the renderer gets the other three directions by rotating this 90 degrees about the sprite centre, so it has to be centred and symmetric about its own axis or it wobbles as it turns — a guarantee arithmetic can make and a diffusion model cannot.

One 16x16 tileable diagonal hatch, authored from the master palette by art/tools/make-zone-overlay.mjs and tinted per zone in code. A zone is a plan, not a machine (plan §5), so it reads as an annotation drawn over the world. Hand-authored because it must tile EXACTLY in both axes and must have binary alpha — the cook stage binarises alpha, so a soft wash would come back opaque and bury the field it annotates.

One 4x4 status lamp, authored from the master palette by art/tools/make-status-lamp.mjs and tinted per state in code. Plan §13: one sprite multiplied by a lamp colour beats five sprites, and it is the only way thirty machines animate state for the cost of one frame.
